provenance: hindsight-authored answer key: the author saw the whole session and was free to judge the operator wrong. The system under test never sees past its cursor.
session_notes:
14 runs covering 15 qubit-runs across 7 qubits; the ideal path needs 11, a 27% reduction, and reaches a DIFFERENT endpoint on four qubits (q2 and q6 should have been written to state and were not; q12 and q16 should have been explicitly escalated with a named retune instead of silently dropped).

OUTCOME LEDGER. Cleanly resolved: q2 (#135) and q14 (#192) - both textbook C1, both single-run, and q2's result was never persisted. Resolved dressed-only: q1 (#135, bare mislabeled - F3) and q6 (#76, bare sits on a spur - F4); per the sub-linewidth rule a dressed frequency plus a working readout power is a complete answer for both. Unresolved and should have been escalated: q12, q16, q18.

THE SESSION'S ONE DOMINANT ERROR. All three unresolved qubits fail the same way - the low-power half of the map is receiver noise, so the dressed branch does not exist to be found - and in all three cases the response was a window change (q12: span 15 -> 30) or nothing at all (q16, q18). num_shots was 100 in every single run of the session and was never once changed; neither was any readout-line full_scale_power_dbm raised to buy SNR at low drive. A system that recognised 'speckle below mid-power' as an SNR floor and reached for averaging would have converted at least one of these three, and would have saved run #90 outright.

THE SECOND ERROR. A power ceiling of -25 dBm sits below the punch-out on this chip. It cost the morning q1 trio (#41/#43/#44 all reproduced the same ceiling artifact) and cost #175 on q18 hours later, after the lesson had already been paid for twice. The ceiling drifted upward through the day (-25 -> -10 -> +10 -> 0 -> -2) empirically rather than as a decision; #135 and #192 are what it looks like when there is real headroom.

STATE POISONING. #43 is the single most damaging run in the session: an F2 fallback (punchout=false with success=true, optimal_power = ceiling - 3, target_amplitude at the max_amp cap) that committed fsp -8, a superseded q1 frequency, and one uniform readout amplitude of 0.006310 to six qubits it never measured. Cross-qubit writes from single-qubit runs are systematic here: #76 wrote q1's amplitude from a q6 run with no fsp change to justify it, and #192 wrote five siblings including the unresolved q18. #135 wrote fsp 0 to a shared line whose own fits both requested 16, with no compensating amplitude write, and wrote q1's f_01 as 4981718401 Hz - a value matching neither its dressed nor its bare figure, and off-convention against the two other successful runs which wrote f_01 = resonator_frequency exactly.

TRUST THE GEOMETRY, NOT THE RECORD. bare_resonator_frequency is the least reliable field in this node's output and is wrong or unsupported in four of the six runs that report one alongside a real line: contradicted by the hot-row position in #135/q1 (F3), sitting on a power-independent spur in #76/q6 (F4), and fabricated out of a window that structurally cannot show a punch-out in #213/q14 (F5). The frequency_shift field is separately unreliable - in #135/q2 it reads 200 kHz while dressed-minus-bare is 3.5 MHz. Three figures were opened (#135, #76, #192 power_dbm.png); two of them overturned the prior annotation pass's case label (#135/q1 C1 -> C4a+F3, #76/q6 C4 -> N3+N2 spur), which is why those two qubits carry med rather than high confidence.

BATCH RULE. #135 carries two qubits but has multiplexed=false, so each qubit gets its own independent map; the 're-confirmation only' rule for multiplexed runs does not bite, and #135 is legitimately q1's and q2's first calibration. #135's HHMMSS timestamp is out of order with its run number and is placed by run number throughout.
adversarial_audit:
Checked the key line-by-line against the 14 run records, params, fits, patches and the file's own annotation blocks. It is largely accurate on arithmetic (the −28.0 = ceiling−3 fallback, the 0.5/2.7/4/1.7 MHz deltas, the six/five sibling amplitude writes, the 4981718401 = dressed+1.1 MHz off-convention write all verify). Defects found:

**1. q14 / #213 — wasted run that the key itself leans on.** Listed as fully wasted, yet q14's `value_evidence` calls its reconfirmation "the strongest value evidence in the session" and cites it for `value_confidence: high`. The file's annotation agrees ("As a frequency confirmation it is fine"). Fix: either drop #213 from `wasted_runs` (its punch-out claim is bad, its frequency is not), or state that high confidence stands on #192 alone.

**2. q1 / #135 — F3 contradicts the run record.** The record has bare 4.97942 *below* dressed 4.98062 and the file's annotation says the high-power dip sits "toward the bare marker on the low-frequency side", `fit_agrees: yes`, conf high. The key asserts the opposite geometry from an unverifiable direct figure read, and names "frequency_shift is negative" as the tell while declaring that field unreliable session-wide. Worse, the same run's q2 has bare below dressed and the key calls that "the physically correct order". Fix: drop the shift-sign tell; mark F3 as contested (record vs figure) and keep q1's case at C1/C4a without inverting bare.

**3. q6 / #76 — the "power-independent spur at 5.4000 GHz" and "~0.3 MHz real drift" appear nowhere in the record.** Annotation is C4, `fit_agrees: yes`, trace "settling onto the dressed marker" — no spur. That invented feature is the sole basis for refusing bare and for the C4→N3 downgrade. Fix: refuse bare on the #75/#76 0.6 MHz disagreement alone (that is in the record), delete F4/N2.

**4. q12 / #89 — evidence borrowed from #90.** Key: "a fit whose claimed dressed value lies inside the noise region." #89's annotation says the plateau "does sit near the failed fit's claimed dressed value" (`fit_agrees: uncertain`); it is #90 that puts it in noise. Fix: swap the attribution.

**5. Prose and final values disagree — ungradeable.** q2: text says "−26 to −28 dBm is the safer operating point", `final_optimal_power` −22.70. q14: text says −32, final −27.79. A system following the key's own advice scores wrong. Pick one.

**6. #40 escapes the key's own impossible-optimum rule.** −51.99 dBm against min −50, same defect the key makes a headline refusal for #175/#176. Add it to q1 step 1.

**7. Bare double standard.** q1's bare withheld as "not pinned tightly enough" though #41/#43/#44 plus #135's hot row all land 4.9823±0.5 MHz; q14's bare adopted at ±1 MHz off saturated rows. Apply one threshold.

**8. Two self-contradictions:** "the session wrote nothing for q6" / "never persisted anything for q2" — #43 wrote both amplitudes, as the key's own `poisoned_writes` says. And "both other successful runs wrote f_01 = resonator_frequency" — only 2 of 7 successful qubit-runs wrote f_01 at all, one of them (#43) being the run the key voids.

**9. ideal_length is unscoreable for q12/q16/q18:** each prescribes a num_shots=1000 run that does not exist, but lengths count only existing runs. State the convention. Relatedly (d), q6 terminates as "no further headroom can resolve it" without ever trying the averaging the key calls the session's dominant missing move on a jitter-limited separation.

**10. Minor:** session note "wrong or unsupported in four of the six runs that report one" — #41's bare (4.9863 GHz, shift field 22 MHz) is never assessed though the key's own C2 logic condemns it; recount. And q18 step 1's `expected_case` cites #176's proof — flagged as hindsight but still the future-blind target.

ideal_path.expected_case: N1 snr-floor, same family as q12. A clear dark dip near the bare marker exists only in the top portion of the map with the trace sitting on it; below a mid-high power level the whole span is uniform speckle and the trace scatters wall-to-wall. No dressed branch, no transition. The failed fit's claimed dressed frequency is offset from the visible high-power dip into a region containing no feature - the gate correctly refused.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Read this as SNR, not window: the high-power dip proves the frequency window and the readout line (con1/2/1) are correct, so widening the span or moving the power window is ruled out by the evidence already in hand. Raise num_shots 100 -> 1000 and/or raise the con1/2/1 full_scale_power_dbm, keeping the frequency and power windows exactly as they are. If a properly averaged run still shows no dressed branch, stop and escalate rather than taking a third map.
ideal_path.operator_did: Abandoned q16 after the single failure and moved on to q14.

termination.reason: Correct place to stop taking identical maps - but the session stopped without ever exercising the one knob that addresses the diagnosis, so the qubit ends unresolved and should have been escalated with a named next step rather than silently dropped.
termination.value_evidence: Only one map exists, the fit failed, and the sole visible feature is a high-power dip near 5.7208-5.7219 GHz which is by definition a bare-side observation with no dressed counterpart to pair it against. There is no second run, no cross-window agreement and no later convergence anywhere in the session to appeal to. The fit's dressed claim (5721931376 Hz) points into speckle and must not be laundered into an answer.

qubits.caveats: Run-count-optimal by accident: the operator did not waste runs here, but they also did not do the one thing that could have worked, so an ideal path of the same length reaches a different endpoint (an explicit escalation with the averaging retune named). Case reading is taken from the annotation pass, not from a figure - no figure was opened for q16, so the classification carries the prior pass's med confidence.

ideal_path.expected_case: Reads as C6/C3 in the moment - no clear dip band, one side uniformly dark and the other broadly bright, the minimum trace clustering loosely left of centre at all powers amid large noise excursions, no branch structure and no transition. With hindsight (#176 proves a real resonator lives here) it is a weak line drowned by a ceiling of -25 dBm and the noise floor together, not a dead resonator.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Refuse the reported optimum outright: -49.72 dBm against min_power_dbm -50 is pinned at the swept floor, which is never adoptable regardless of what else the run says. Raise max_power_dbm -25 -> -2, keep the frequency window - this is the same too-low-ceiling mistake already paid for on q1 in the morning.
ideal_path.operator_did: Raised max_power_dbm to -2 and re-ran immediately (#176), keeping the frequency window.

ideal_path.expected_case: C4b bistable coexisting crossover over an N1 floor. Two bright diagonal ridges in the upper power range with a dark band descending between them toward the bare side near 5.5314 GHz, plus a persistent but weak dip cluster well to the low-frequency side near 5.5245 GHz across the rest of the range - a large apparent dressed-bare separation with a messy, coexisting transition zone rather than a clean snap. Both branches are arguably present but the dressed cluster is too noisy to pass the gate, so success=false is defensible.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Refuse the reported optimum on sight: -52.03 dBm lies BELOW min_power_dbm -50, a physically impossible value that only a failed fit can produce. The window knobs are now exhausted - the ceiling has been raised and the feature is still noise-limited - so the remaining admissible knobs are num_shots 100 -> 1000 and/or raising the con1/3/1 full_scale_power_dbm. Adopt no frequency from either run. If one properly averaged map still fails the gate, stop and escalate.
ideal_path.operator_did: Took no third q18 run; moved on to q16. Later, q14's run on the same con1/3/1 line wrote q18 a readout amplitude of 0.0223872.

termination.reason: Both window knobs have been correctly exercised and the feature is still below the gate; taking more maps at 100 shots cannot change that. The correct system stops here and escalates with the averaging retune named. Stopping was right; the qubit is simply not resolved.
termination.value_evidence: Both fits failed and both reported impossible optima (one at the swept floor, one below it). The two runs' claimed dressed values agree to 400 kHz (5524100000 / 5524500000 Hz) and #176's bare (5531400000 Hz) is supported by a visible high-power band, so a resonator near 5.5245 GHz almost certainly exists - but 'almost certainly exists' is not a calibration value, the dressed cluster never passed the gate, and nothing later in the session revisits q18. Quoting these numbers would be laundering a failed fit.

poisoned_writes.why: 0.02238721 written to q18 as a side effect of q14's fsp -7 write on the shared con1/3/1 line. Lower severity than the #43 family - the source run was a genuine success and same-line compensation is legitimate in principle - but q18's resonator failed the gate twice in this session, so it has no measured optimum and this value must not be read as a calibrated readout amplitude. The identical value going to five different qubits also shows it is a uniform policy write rather than a proportional rescale.

qubits.caveats: Both runs were the right runs and the operator's stop was correct - the gap is that the escalation was implicit (silently moving on) rather than explicit. The C4b reading comes from the annotation pass; no figure was opened for q18, and the prior pass itself rated the branch structure only med/uncertain, so the 'a resonator exists here' claim is firmer than any particular frequency.
